docs.title: Создание документа на основе готового шаблона
docs.text:
1. Находясь в элементе сущности (например, в конкретной сделке), нажмите на выпадающий список «Ещё» в меню действий над таймлайном.

  2. Выберите пункт «Новый документ».

  3. Укажите шаблон, который необходимо заполнить.

  4. Дождитесь, пока данные подгрузятся в шаблон, и нажмите кнопку «Готово» в правом верхнем углу.

  5. Введите имя документа и нажмите «ОК».

  6. Созданный документ отобразится в таймлайне.

docs.title: Настройка меню
docs.text:
Меню действий над таймлайном можно настраивать. Кнопку «Новый документ» удобно вынести в основное меню, чтобы не заходить каждый раз в раздел «Ещё».

Для этого:

  1. Откройте список «Ещё».

  2. Нажмите «Настроить меню».

  3. Зажмите левой кнопкой мыши пункт «Новый документ» и перетащите его в основное меню.

  4. Завершите настройку.

После этого кнопка будет доступна сразу в панели действий.

docs.title: Creating a template
docs.text:
After completing the app setup, you can create a template.

A template is created from the Bitrix24 entity where it will be used. For example, to create a template for deals, open any deal card.

docs.title: Opening Kombinator Templates
docs.text:
1. Open the required Bitrix24 entity, for example Deals.

  2. Open any card within the selected entity.

  3. In the card menu, select «Kombinator Templates».

    If the item is not displayed in the main menu, open «More».

    To pin the item to the main menu, click «Configure menu», click and hold «Kombinator Templates», and drag it to the required position. Then finish editing the menu.

    If «Kombinator Templates» is not available in either the main menu or the «More» section, go to app setup and make sure the required entity is enabled.

docs.title: Creating a new template
docs.text:
1. Open the «Kombinator Templates» tab and click «New template».

  2. Enter the template name and click «OK».

  3. Open the «File» tab, click «Open», and select the DOCX document you want to convert into a template.

docs.title: Adding fields
docs.text:
«Fields» is the panel on the left side of the editor. It contains the fields whose data can be used to populate the template.

  1. Click the three-dot menu next to the required entity, for example Deals, and select «Edit fields».

  2. In the window that opens, find the required fields using search or by scrolling through the list.

  3. Select the fields you want to add to «Fields» and click «OK».

Note. Custom Bitrix24 fields have the UF_CRM_ prefix.

docs.title: Adding fields to the document
docs.text:
To insert a field into the document:

  1. Place the cursor where you want to insert the field.

  2. Find the required field in «Fields».

  3. Click the three-dot menu next to the field.

  4. Select the required insertion method.

docs.title: Working with fields in the document
docs.text:
Example:

Your browser does not support video playback.

Fields can be inserted into the document using Expression, Condition expression, Switch, For, or Table.

Before inserting a field, check its type and whether it is nested inside a list.

docs.title: How to identify a field type
docs.text:
The field type is displayed below the field name in «Fields».

For example:

  • Product name — Text;
  • Price — Decimal;
  • Products — List;
  • Product — Struct.

Field nesting is indicated by indentation. The farther a field is shifted to the right, the deeper it is nested in the structure.

docs.title: Insertion methods
docs.text:
Insertion method How it works Applicable field types Insert «Expression» Inserts the field value or the result of an expression into the document Text, number, date Insert «Condition expression» Controls whether a document fragment is displayed. The fragment is included only when the specified condition is met Boolean Insert «For» Creates a repeating section. Text and fields from list items can be placed inside it, and the content is repeated for each item List Insert «Table» Repeats table rows for list items. Fields from each list item can be inserted into the cells of the repeated rows List

Note. Each field type supports a specific set of functions. The table above includes links to the corresponding field type articles, where the available functions are listed.

docs.title: «Marker must be inside…» error
docs.text:
The «Marker must be inside…» message appears when a field is nested inside a list but is inserted into the document outside that list.

For example, if you try to insert the Product Name field outside a For or Table marker, the following message will appear:

Marker must be inside Products.

This means that Product name is nested inside the Products list.

In this case:

  1. Insert Products using For or Table.

  2. Place the cursor inside the inserted structure.

  3. Insert Product name using Expression.

If a similar message then appears with the name of another list, the field is nested inside multiple lists. Add a separate For or Table marker for each list, starting with the outermost list and moving inward.

After creating the template:

  • if the document should be generated automatically using Bitrix24 automation rules or business processes, proceed to template automation;
  • if automation is not required, proceed to generating a document.

docs.title: App installation
docs.text:
1. Open Market.

  2. Enter «Kombinator» in the search bar and open the app from the search results.

  3. Click «Install».

  4. In the window that opens, review the app terms of use and click «Install».

  5. Once the installation is complete, click «Open» nd proceed to the app setup.

docs.title: Integration
docs.text:
Integration determines which Bitrix24 entity cards will display the Kombinator app.

  1. Open the «Integration» tab.

  2. Select the entities where the app should be available.

  3. Click «Save».

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
The «Roles» tab is used to configure sets of permissions that can then be assigned to Kombinator users.

The Administrator, Designer, and Editor roles are created by default. If needed, you can create a custom role and specify which actions are available to it.

Default roles

  1. Designer — provides access to view and edit templates, as well as organization administrator permissions.

    The following permissions are enabled:

    • Templates — Read;
    • Templates — Edit;
    • Team admin.

  2. Editor — provides read-only access to templates.

    The following permission is enabled:

    • Templates — Read.

  3. The Administrator role is also created by default.

Adding a role

To create a custom role:

  1. Open the «Roles» tab.

  2. Click «Add».

  3. Enter the role name.

  4. Select the required permissions:

    • Templates — Read — allows users to view templates;
    • Templates — Edit — allows users to edit templates;
    • Team admin — grants organization administrator permissions.

  5. Click «Save».

The created role can then be assigned to an employee in the «User Accounts» tab.

docs.title: Accounts
docs.text:
Accounts — are Bitrix24 employees who have access to the Kombinator app.

  1. Open the «Accounts» tab.

  2. Click «Add».

  3. In the «User» field, select the required employee.

  4. Assign the required roles and click «Save».

Once the setup is complete, proceed to creating a template.

docs.title: Template automation
docs.text:
Document generation from a template can be automated using a Bitrix24 automation rule.

An automation rule can be added:

  • to CRM automation — the document will be generated when an item moves to a specific stage;

  • to a workflow — the document will be generated when the workflow reaches the corresponding action.

Before setting up automation, make sure the document template has been created and saved, and that Kombinator is connected to the required Bitrix24 entity.

docs.title: Adding an automation rule to CRM
docs.text: The automation rule generates a document when a CRM item moves to the stage where the rule is configured.

docs.title: Adding the automation rule
docs.text:
1. Go to CRM.

  2. Open the required entity, for example Deals.

  3. Open the «Automation rules» tab.

  4. Select the required pipeline.

  5. At the stage where the document should be generated, click «+ add».

  6. In the «Other» group, find «[Document Builder — Kombinator] Create a document».

  7. Click «Add».

  8. In the window that opens, configure the conditions, execution order, and execution time.

  9. In «Robot settings», select the template that should be used to generate the document.

docs.title: Setting up the file name mask
docs.text:
1. Expand «Name mask settings».

  2. By default, the mask field contains the name of the selected template in double quotation marks. If you leave the settings unchanged, this name will be used as the document name.

  3. If needed, change how the document name is generated:

    • if the file name mask is already configured in the template, enable «Use the name mask from the template»;

    • if no mask is configured in the template, enter it directly in the automation rule settings;

    • if no separate mask is required, leave the default template name.

The file name mask field cannot be empty.

docs.title: Saving the document to Drive
docs.text:
By default, the generated document is attached to the item timeline. You can also save it to Bitrix24 Drive.

  1. Enable «Save document to Drive».

  2. Select where the document should be saved: a shared drive or a personal drive.

  3. Enter the folder name. The automation rule will check whether a folder with this name already exists on the selected drive:

    • if the folder exists, documents will be saved there;

    • if the folder does not exist, it will be created automatically.

  4. Select the file formats that should be saved to Drive.

docs.title: Completing the setup
docs.text:
1. Select the employee whose account will be used to run the automation rule.

  2. Click «Save».

The automation rule will now generate a document whenever a CRM item moves to the selected stage.

docs.title: Adding Kombinator to a workflow
docs.text:
Kombinator can also generate documents as part of a Bitrix24 workflow.

The settings are similar to those of the CRM automation rule. The main difference is how document generation is triggered: in CRM automation, the rule runs when an item moves to a specific stage, while in a workflow the document is generated when the workflow reaches the corresponding action.

docs.title: Creating a workflow
docs.text:
1. Go to «Automation».

  2. Open «Workflows» and select «Workflows in CRM».

  3. Select the CRM entity for which you want to configure document generation, for example Deals.

  4. Click «Add Template».

  5. Enter the workflow name.

  6. If needed, configure Autorun:

    • «When added» — the workflow starts when a new CRM item is created;

    • «When changed» — the workflow starts when a CRM item is modified.

    If Autorun is not enabled, the workflow can be started manually from the CRM item.

  7. Save the settings and open the Workflow Designer.

docs.title: Adding the Kombinator action
docs.text:
In a workflow, document generation is added as a separate action.

  1. Click the arrow at the point in the workflow where the document should be generated.

  2. In the list of actions, select «Application Actions» → «[Document Builder — Kombinator] Create a document».

  3. Click the gear icon next to the added action to open its settings.

  4. Configure the action in the same way as the CRM automation rule: select the template, specify the file name mask, storage location, and document format.

  5. Select the employee whose account will be used to run the action.

  6. Save the action settings and the workflow template.

In a workflow, you do not need to separately specify the CRM stage, execution order, or execution time. The action runs according to its position and the logic configured in the workflow.

docs.title: Expression
docs.text: The «Expression» directive is used to insert a field value or the result of an expression into the document. It can insert text, numbers, dates, calculation results, or function results.

docs.title: Expression
docs.text:
When adding the directive, specify the expression whose result should be inserted into the document.

For a regular field, enter its identifier:

customerName

For a nested field, specify the full path using a period (.):

deals.fullName

You can also use more complex expressions, for example:

  • a calculation — quantity * price;
  • a function — formatDate(contractDate, "dd.MM.yyyy");
  • concatenation — "Contract № " & contractNumber;
  • a conditional function — if(...).

Expression syntax is described in «Basic rules».

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
The «Expression» directive is not intended for repeating list items. Use the «For» or «Table» directive for lists.

To show or hide part of the document depending on a condition, use the «Condition expression» directive.

docs.title: External
docs.text:
The «External» directive is used to insert content from one template into another.

This allows you to reuse the same document sections without copying them. If the external template is updated, the changes will be applied wherever that template is used.

docs.title: Adding an external template
docs.text:
To add content from another template:

  1. Place the cursor where you want to insert the content.

  2. On the «Directives» tab, select «External».

  3. Select the template whose content you want to insert.

When the document is generated, the content of the selected template will be inserted at the position of the directive.

docs.title: Passing values to an external template
docs.text:
If the main template and the external template use fields with the same identifiers, no additional configuration is required.

For example, if both templates use the field:

counterparty

the field value will also be available in the external template.

If the field identifiers are different, configure a parameter to pass the required value.

For example:

  • the field in the external template has the identifier contractor;
  • the required value in the main template is stored in the counterparty field.

In this case, specify:

Parameter name — the field identifier in the external template:

contractor

Parameter expression — the field or expression from the main template whose value should be passed:

counterparty

As a result, the contractor field in the external template will receive the value of the counterparty field from the main template.

docs.title: Fields used in the external template
docs.text: If the external template uses fields that are not included in Fields of the main template and their values are not passed through parameters, add those fields to Fields in the main template.

docs.title: For
docs.text:
The «For» directive is used to repeat part of a document for each item in a list.

For example, it can be used to display products, services, employees, or other data from a List field.

docs.title: What the For directive is used for
docs.text:
A List field can contain multiple items. For example:

Product 1

Name: Laptop
Quantity: 2
Price: 80,000

Product 2

Name: Monitor
Quantity: 3
Price: 25,000

Product 3

Name: Keyboard
Quantity: 5
Price: 4,000

You do not need to create a separate block for each product.

Configure the For directive once, and Kombinator will process each item in the list and repeat the content for it.

The number of repetitions depends on the number of items in the list. If the list contains 10 products, the content inside the directive is repeated 10 times. If the list is empty, the content inside the directive is not included in the document.

docs.title: Adding and structuring the directive
docs.text:
1. Place the cursor where the repeating block should begin and select «Directives» → «For» → «For».

    In the directive settings, specify:

    • Row variable — the name used to reference the current list item;
    • Source — the List field whose items should be processed;
    • Separator — optional text or a character inserted between repeated blocks.

    After the directive is added, the opening part is inserted:

    text {for(productData in productList)}

  2. After the opening part, add the text and other directives that should be repeated for each list item.

  3. Close the construction with {/for}.

The complete construction may look like this:

{for(productData in productList)}

Product: productData.name

Quantity: productData.quantity

Unit price: productData.price

{/for}

docs.title: Current list item
docs.text:
Inside the For directive, a variable is used to reference the current item in the list.

By default, this name is the identifier of the composite field that represents a list item.

For example, if the composite field identifier is productData, its nested fields can be referenced as:

productData.name
productData.quantity
productData.price

You can change the current item variable and use another valid name.

For example:

{for(product in productList)}

In this case, the nested fields must also be referenced using the new variable:

product.name
product.quantity
product.price

docs.title: «For» and «Table»
docs.text:
Both directives are used to work with data from a List field, but they are intended for different output formats.

Use «For» when you need to repeat any document fragment for each list item, such as text, several lines, a paragraph, or a block containing other directives.

Use the «Table» directive when list items should be displayed as table rows.

docs.title: Condition expression
docs.text:
The «Condition expression» directive controls which content is included in the generated document depending on a specified condition.

Kombinator evaluates the condition and either includes or excludes the content inside the directive.

For example, you can:

  • include a contract clause only when a field has a specific value;
  • display additional text when an amount exceeds a specified value;
  • display one version of the content when the condition is met and another when it is not.

docs.title: Directive structure
docs.text:
The directive consists of an opening and a closing part.

The condition is specified in the opening part:

{if (condition)}

Content to be included.

{/if}

Kombinator evaluates the expression specified in the opening part.

If the result is true, the content between If and /Endif is included in the document.

If the result is false, the content is not included.

docs.title: Condition
docs.text:
The condition must be an expression that returns the Boolean value true or false.

For example, you can check a numeric field:

amount > 100000

If the amount field contains a value greater than 100000, the condition is met.

You can compare field values:

quantity > limit

check text values:

status = "Approved"

or check whether a value is present:

contractNumber != null

Logical operators and functions can also be used according to the general expression syntax.

For more information, see «Basic rules».

docs.title: Boolean field
docs.text:
A Boolean field can be used directly as a condition.

For example:

delivery

If the delivery field contains true, the condition is met and the content inside the directive is included in the document.

If the field contains false, the content is excluded.

To check the opposite value, use the not operator:

not delivery

In this case, the content will be included when the delivery field contains false.

docs.title: Multiple conditions
docs.text:
A single expression can contain multiple conditions.

Use the and operator when both conditions must be true:

amount > 100000 and approval

The content will be included only if the amount is greater than 100000 and the approval field returns true.

Use the or operator when at least one condition must be true:

urgentOrder or importantClient

The content will be included if at least one of these conditions is met.

docs.title: Else block
docs.text:
Use the Else block when you need two content options: one for a true condition and another for a false condition.

The structure is:

{if (condition)}

Content displayed when the condition is true.

{else}

Content displayed when the condition is false.

{/if}

For example:

{if (amount > 100000)}

Additional approval is required.

{else}

Additional approval is not required.

{/if}

If amount > 100000, the first content block is included in the document.

If the condition is not met, the content after Else is included.

The Else block is optional. If no alternative content is required, use only If and /Endif.

docs.title: Nested conditions
docs.text:
One «Condition expression» directive can be placed inside another. This allows you to check several dependent conditions step by step.

For example:

{if (delivery)}

Delivery terms.

    {if (urgentDelivery)}

    Delivery within one business day.

    {/if}

{/if}

Kombinator first checks the delivery field.

Only if this condition is met does it evaluate the nested urgentDelivery condition.

docs.title: Picture
docs.text:
The «Picture» directive is used to insert an image into a document.

You can specify the field from which Kombinator should retrieve the image, set its size, and choose how the image should be resized while preserving its original proportions.

docs.title: Directive parameters
docs.text:
When adding the «Picture» directive, specify the following parameters:

  • Expression — a Picture field from which Kombinator retrieves the image;

  • Image height — the image height in centimeters. The default value is 3 cm;

  • Image width — the image width in centimeters. The default value is 3 cm;

  • Resize mode — determines how the image is resized relative to the specified height and width.

docs.title: Resize modes
docs.text:
When the image is resized, its original proportions are preserved.

Three resize modes are available.

docs.title: By height
docs.text:
The image height is set to the value specified in Image height. The width is calculated automatically to preserve the original proportions.

In this mode, the specified width does not limit the image size.

For example, if the following values are set:

Height — 3 cm
Width — 4 cm

but the proportional width is 6 cm when the image height is 3 cm, the resulting image size will be 3 × 6 cm.

docs.title: By width
docs.text:
The image width is set to the value specified in Image width. The height is calculated automatically to preserve the original proportions.

In this mode, the specified height does not limit the image size.

For example, if the following values are set:

Height — 3 cm
Width — 4 cm

but the proportional height is 5 cm when the image width is 4 cm, the resulting image size will be 5 × 4 cm.

docs.title: By height and width
docs.text:
The image is resized proportionally so that neither its height nor its width exceeds the specified values.

For example, if the following values are set:

Height — 3 cm
Width — 5 cm

the image will be fitted within 3 × 5 cm. Depending on its original proportions, one side may be smaller than the specified value.

docs.title: Picture directive in the template
docs.text:
After the directive is added, a placeholder image appears in the template. It shows the position and size of the image that will be inserted into the generated document.

You can resize the placeholder directly in the editor. The updated height and width are saved and used when the document is generated.

The image is placed inline with text, so its position depends on where the directive is located in the template.

When the document is generated, the placeholder is replaced with the image from the field specified in Expression.

docs.title: Switch
docs.text:
The «Switch» directive is used when the document should display one of several content options depending on a field value.

Kombinator retrieves the specified field value, compares it with the configured Case values, and inserts the content of the matching block.

For example, depending on the counterpartyType field, you can display different text for an LLC, a sole proprietor, or an individual.

docs.title: Directive structure
docs.text:
The directive consists of:

  • an opening «Switch» directive — specifies the field or expression whose value should be checked;
  • one or more «Case» blocks — define content for specific values;
  • an optional «Default» block — defines content to use when no Case value matches;
  • a closing «/Switch» directive.

Общая структура:

{switch(field)}

{case("Value 1")}

Content for the first value.

{case("Value 2")}

Content for the second value.

{default}

Content displayed if no value matches.

{/switch}

docs.title: Value to check
docs.text:
In the opening «Switch» directive, specify the field whose value Kombinator should compare with the Case values.

For example:

counterpartyType

To reference a nested field, specify the full path using a period (.):

counterparty.type

Field reference rules are described in «Basic rules».

docs.title: «Case» block
docs.text:
dd a separate «Case» block for each value that should display its own content.

For example:

{switch(counterpartyType)}

{case("LLC")}

Text for a legal entity.

{case("Sole proprietor")}

Text for a sole proprietor.

{case("Individual")}

Text for an individual.

{/switch}

If the counterpartyType field contains "Sole proprietor", only the content of the corresponding Case block will be included in the document:

Text for a sole proprietor.

The value specified in «Case» must exactly match the value of the field being checked.

For text values, letter case is taken into account. For example, "LLC" and "llc" are treated as different values.

docs.title: «Default» block
docs.text:
Use «Default» when you need to display content if none of the Case values match the field value.

For example:

{switch(counterpartyType)}

{case("LLC")}

Legal entity.

{case("Sole proprietor")}

Sole proprietor.

{default}

Other counterparty type.

{/switch}

If the field value does not match either "LLC" or "Sole proprietor", the document will contain:

Other counterparty type.

The «Default» block is optional. If it is not added and no matching Case is found, nothing is inserted at the position of the directive.

docs.title: «Switch» and «Condition expression»
docs.text:
The «Switch» and «Condition expression» directives both control which content is included in the document, but they are used for different tasks.

Use «Switch» when one field can contain several possible values and each value should display different content.

For example:

LLC
Sole proprietor
Individual

Use «Condition expression» when you need to evaluate a logical expression:

amount > 100000

or combine several conditions:

amount > 100000 и approval

If you need to select one of several content options based on the value of a single field, use «Switch».

docs.title: Table
docs.text:
The «Table» directive is used to control table rows when generating a document.

It allows you to repeat rows for list items, display rows only when a condition is met, and vertically merge adjacent cells.

docs.title: Table for
docs.text: «Table for» is used to display data from a List field in a table.

docs.title: Table for structure
docs.text:
The opening directive has the following structure:

{t_for(employee in employeeList)}

Где:

Where:

  • employeeList — the List field whose items should be processed;
  • employee — the name used to reference the current list item.

If a list item is a composite field, its nested fields are referenced using a period (.):

employee.fullName
employee.position
employee.workExperience

The current item variable can be changed.

For example:

{t_for(data in employeeList)}

In this case, the nested fields must also be referenced using the new variable:

data.fullName
data.position
data.workExperience

The Table for block must be closed with:

{/t_for}

The opening t_for and closing /t_for directives must each be placed in a separate table row.

Do not add text, values, or other directives to the rows containing t_for and /t_for. These rows are used only to define the beginning and end of the repeating table block.

docs.title: Which rows are repeated
docs.text:
Table for repeats the entire table block located between t_for and /t_for.

For one list item, the repeating block may contain a single row:

or multiple rows:

The repeating block can also contain other directives and additional logic:

For example, if the block contains three rows, all three rows will be generated for each item in the list.

Therefore, the number of rows in the generated table depends not only on the number of list items but also on the structure placed inside Table for.

docs.title: Table if
docs.text:
«Table if» controls whether specific table rows are included in the generated document.

Rows placed between t_if and /t_if are included only when the specified condition is met.

docs.title: Table if structure
docs.text:
Table if consists of an opening t_if directive containing a condition and a closing /t_if directive.

For example:

{t_if(data.workExperience > 3)}

...

{/t_if}

If the expression data.workExperience > 3 returns истина, the rows inside the block are included in the document.

If it returns ложь, the rows are not included.

A Boolean field or a logical expression can be used as the condition.

The opening t_if and closing /t_if directives must each be placed in a separate table row.

Do not add text, values, or other directives to the rows containing t_if and /t_if. These rows are used only to define the beginning and end of the conditional block.

docs.title: Table if inside Table for
docs.text:
Table if can be placed inside Table for to evaluate a condition separately for each list item.

The structure may look like this:

Table for processes all employees in the list, while Table if checks the condition for each employee individually.

Rows containing employee data will be generated only for employees for whom the condition data.workExperience > 3 is met.

docs.title: V_Merge
docs.text:
«V_Merge» is used to merge adjacent table cells vertically.

Place the directive inside a cell in the column where the cells should be merged.

docs.title: How V_Merge works
docs.text:
The directive contains an expression:

v_merge(expression)

When the document is generated, Kombinator compares the result of this expression in adjacent rows.

If the results are the same, the corresponding cells are merged vertically. When the result changes, a new group begins.

For example:

v_merge(data.type)

If data.type contains the following values:

Installation
Installation
Installation
Delivery
Delivery

docs.title: Today
docs.text:
The Today function returns the current date at the time the document is generated.

The function is useful when you need to automatically insert the current date into a document or use it in calculations.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
Today()

Parameters:

The function does not accept any parameters.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns the current date with the time set to 00:00:00.

For example, if the document is generated on September 2, 2026:

Today()

Result:

02.09.2026 00:00:00

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
The function value is determined at the time the document is generated.

Therefore, if the same template is generated on different days, Today() returns the corresponding generation date.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Using the current date in a calculation*

The current date can be used as the source value for other functions.

For example:

edate(Today(), 1)

If the document is generated on September 2, 2026, the result is:

02.10.2026 00:00:00

Calculating the difference between dates

The function can be used to calculate the number of days between the current date and another date:

datediff(Today(), endDate)

The result depends on the value of endDate.

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
The result of Today can be used with other date functions.

For example, you can immediately display the current date in the required format:

formatDate(Today(),"dddd, d MMMM yyyy","en")

If the document is generated on September 22, 2026, the result is:

Tuesday, 22 September 2026

The Today function can also be combined with date calculation functions such as edate, bomonth, eomonth, and datediff.

docs.title: bomonth
docs.text:
The bomonth function returns the first day of a month based on the specified offset from the source date.

The function is useful when you need to determine the beginning of the current, previous, or future month.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
bomonth(sourceDate, numberOfMonths)

Parameters:

  • sourceDate — the date used as the starting point for calculating the beginning of the month. Required;
  • numberOfMonths — the number of months to shift. Required numeric parameter.

A positive value shifts the calculation forward, a negative value shifts it backward, and 0 uses the month of the source date.

You can use:

  • field values;
  • results of other functions;
  • expressions.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns the date of the first day of the calculated month.

If the source date contains a time value, the time is preserved.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
Regardless of the day in the source date, the function returns the first day of the calculated month.

For example:

bomonth("15/04/2025", 0)

Result:

01.04.2025 00:00:00

With a negative offset, the function returns the first day of a previous month.

For example:

bomonth("15/04/2025", -1)

Result:

01.03.2025 00:00:00

The function accepts fractional numeric values.

For example:

bomonth("15/04/2025", 1.5)

Result:

01.06.2025 00:00:00

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Shifting by several months

bomonth("15/04/2025", 2)

Result:

01.06.2025 00:00:00

Using an expression

If:

  • sourceDate = 15/04/2025;
  • numberOfMonths = 1;

the expression:

bomonth(sourceDate, numberOfMonths + 1)

returns:

01.06.2025 00:00:00

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The function returns an error if one of the required parameters is empty.

An error occurs if no value is provided for:

  • sourceDate;
  • numberOfMonths.

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
The bomonth function can be combined with other date functions.

You can create the source date using the date function and then determine the beginning of the required month:

bomonth(date(15, 4, 2025), 2)

Result:

01.06.2025 00:00:00

The result can be passed to a formatting function:

formatDate(bomonth(date(15, 4, 2026), 6),"dddd, d MMMM yyyy","en")

Result:

Thursday, 1 October 2026

docs.title: date
docs.text:
The date function creates a date from separately specified day, month, and year values.

The function is useful when the parts of a date are stored in different fields or calculated directly in an expression.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
date(day, month, year)

Parameters:

  • day — day of the month. Required. A numeric value from 1 to 31;
  • month — month number. Required. A numeric value from 1 to 12;
  • year — year. Required. Specified as a number, for example 2026.

Parameters must be specified in the following order: day, month, year.

You can use:

  • numbers;
  • values from numeric fields;
  • numeric expressions.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns a date value.

Because hours, minutes, and seconds are not specified, the time is set to 00:00:00.

For example:

date(12, 8, 2026)

Result:

12.08.2026 00:00:00

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
The specified values must form a valid calendar date.

The day parameter can contain a value from 1 to 31, but the maximum valid value depends on the selected month and year.

If a fractional numeric value is passed, the function converts it when creating the date.

For example:

date(1.5, 5, 2026)

Result:

02.05.2026 00:00:00

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Values from fields

If the fields contain:

  • day = 5;
  • month = 9;
  • year = 2026;

the expression:

date(day, month, year)

returns:

05.09.2026 00:00:00

Using an expression

Calculations can be used in function parameters.

If the fields contain:

  • day = 5;
  • month = 9;
  • year = 2026;

the expression:

date(day + 1, month, year)

returns:

06.09.2026 00:00:00

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The function returns an error if the specified values cannot form a valid date.

For example:

date(31, 2, 2026)

returns an error because February 2026 does not have 31 days.

An error also occurs if:

  • day is 0;
  • the month number is greater than 12;
  • the specified day does not exist in the selected month and year;
  • one of the required parameters is empty.

For example:

date(29, 2, 2025)

returns an error because 2025 does not have February 29.

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
The date function can be combined with other date functions.

A date created with date can be:

  • split into individual parts using day, month, and year;
  • used to retrieve calendar information such as the weekday or week number;
  • passed to date formatting functions.

The date function can also be used to create a new date based on an existing one.

For example:

date(day(sourceDate), month(sourceDate), year(sourceDate) + 1)

This expression keeps the day and month from sourceDate and increases the year by 1.

The resulting date can also be passed directly to formatDate:

formatDate(date(5, 9, 2026), "yyyy-MM-dd")

Result:

2026-09-05

This allows date to be used as part of a more complex expression: first create or modify a date, then extract the required information or change how the date is displayed.

docs.title: datediff
docs.text:
The datediff function returns the difference between two dates in days.

The function is useful when you need to determine the duration of a period between two dates, for example, the number of days between the start and end of an event or document.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
datediff(startDate, endDate)

Parameters:

  • startDate — the date from which the difference is calculated. Required;
  • endDate — the date up to which the difference is calculated. Required.

You can use:

  • field values;
  • results of other functions;
  • expressions.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns a numeric value representing the difference between the dates in days.

The sign of the result depends on the order of the dates:

  • if endDate is later than startDate, the result is positive;
  • if endDate is earlier than startDate, the result is negative;
  • if the dates are the same, the result is 0.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
The order of the parameters affects the result.

For example:

datediff("31/03/2025", "04/06/2025")

Result:

65

If the dates are reversed:

datediff("04/06/2025", "31/03/2025")

Result:

-65

If the dates are the same, the function returns 0:

datediff("15/04/2025", "15/04/2025")

Result:

0

The function also accepts date and time values.

For example:

datediff("15/04/2025 12:00:00","16/04/2025 00:00:00")

Result:

0

In this example, the difference between the values is less than one full day, so the function returns 0.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Calculating the number of days between dates

datediff("15/04/2025", "16/04/2025")

Result:

1

Using results of other functions

Dates created by other functions can be passed as parameters:

datediff(date(15, 4, 2025), date(20, 4, 2025))

Result:

5

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The function returns an error if one of the required parameters is empty.

An error occurs if no value is provided for:

  • startDate;
  • endDate.

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
The datediff function can be combined with other date functions.

For example, you can calculate the number of days between today's date and a date shifted by one month:

datediff(today(), edate(today(), 1))

In the tested example, the result is:

30

The dates can also be created using the date function:

datediff(date(15, 4, 2025), date(20, 4, 2025))

Result:

5

This allows datediff to be used as part of a more complex expression when the start or end date is determined by another function.

docs.title: dateshift
docs.text:
The dateshift function shifts a source date forward or backward by the specified number of days.

The function is useful when you need to calculate a date relative to another date, for example, to determine a deadline several days later or get a date from a previous period.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
dateshift(sourceDate, numberOfDays)

Parameters:

  • sourceDate — the date from which the shift is calculated. Required;
  • numberOfDays — the number of days by which the date should be shifted. Required numeric parameter.

A positive numberOfDays value shifts the date forward, while a negative value shifts it backward. A value of 0 returns the source date without shifting it.

You can use:

  • field values;
  • results of other functions;
  • expressions.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns a date shifted by the specified number of days.

If the source date contains a time value, the time is preserved.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
The function automatically handles transitions between months and years.

For example:

dateshift("31/12/2025", 1)

Result:

01.01.2026 00:00:00

If the source date contains a time value, the time is preserved after the shift.

For example:

dateshift("31/03/2025 14:30:25", 1)

Result:

01.04.2025 14:30:25

The function accepts fractional numeric values.

For example:

dateshift("31/03/2025", 1.5)

Result:

02.04.2025 00:00:00

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Shifting a date forward

dateshift("31/03/2025", 20)

Result:

20.04.2025 00:00:00

Shifting a date backward

dateshift("31/03/2025", -20)

Result:

11.03.2025 00:00:00

Using a field value and an expression

If:

  • sourceDate = 02/09/2026;
  • numberOfDays = 3;

the expression:

dateshift(sourceDate, numberOfDays + 1)

returns:

06.09.2026 00:00:00

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The function returns an error if one of the required parameters is empty.

An error occurs if no value is provided for:

  • sourceDate;
  • numberOfDays.

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
The dateshift function can be combined with other date functions.

You can create the source date using the date function and then shift it by the required number of days:

dateshift(date(31, 3, 2025), 20)

Result:

20.04.2025 00:00:00

The result can be passed to a formatting function:

formatDate(dateshift(date(31, 3, 2025), 20),"dddd, d MMMM yyyy","en")

Result:

Sunday, 20 April 2025

docs.title: datetime
docs.text:
The datetime function creates a single date and time value from separately specified year, month, day, hour, minute, and second values.

The function is useful when the parts of a date and time are stored in different fields or calculated directly in an expression.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
datetime(year, month, day, hours, minutes, seconds)

Parameters:

  • year — year. Required numeric parameter;
  • month — month number. Required numeric parameter. A value from 1 to 12;
  • day — day of the month. Required numeric parameter. A value from 1 to 31;
  • hours — hours. Required numeric parameter. A value from 0 to 23;
  • minutes — minutes. Required numeric parameter. A value from 0 to 59;
  • seconds — seconds. Required numeric parameter. A value from 0 to 59.

Parameters must be specified in the following order: year, month, day, hours, minutes, seconds.

You can use:

  • numbers;
  • values from numeric fields;
  • results of other functions;
  • expressions.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns a date and time value.

For example:

datetime(2026, 8, 11, 14, 30, 15)

Result:

11.08.2026 14:30:15

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
The specified values must form a valid date and time.

Fractional numeric values may be converted when the result is created, so it is recommended to use integers for the parameters.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Using field values and an expression

If the fields contain:

  • year = 2026;
  • month = 8;
  • day = 10;
  • hours = 14;
  • minutes = 30;
  • seconds = 15;

the expression:

datetime(
    year,
    month,
    day + 1,
    hours,
    minutes,
    seconds
)

returns:

11.08.2026 14:30:15

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The function returns an error if the specified values cannot form a valid date and time.

For example:

datetime(2026, 2, 31, 14, 30, 15)

returns an error because February 2026 does not have 31 days.

An error also occurs if one of the parameter values is outside the allowed range.

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
The datetime function can be combined with functions that extract individual parts of a date and time.

For example, you can extract all components from an existing date and time value and create a new one:

datetime(year(now()), month(now()), day(now()), hour(now()), minute(now()), second(now()))

To display the resulting value in a custom format, use formatDate:

formatDate(datetime(2026, 8, 11, 14, 30, 15), "dd MMMM yyyy 'at' HH:mm","en")

Result:

11 August 2026 at 14:30

docs.title: day
docs.text:
The day function returns the day of the month from a specified date.

The function is useful when you need to extract the day from a full date value and use it separately in a document or expression.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
day(date)

Parameters:

  • date — the date from which the day of the month should be extracted. Required.

You can use:

  • a date field value;
  • the result of another function that returns a date;
  • an expression whose result is a date.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns the day of the month as a number from 1 to 31.

For example:

day("11/08/2026")

Result:

11

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Getting the day from a field value

If the contractDate field contains:

11/08/2026

the expression:

day(contractDate)

returns:

11

Getting the current day of the month

You can get the current day from the result of Today():

day(Today())

If the document is generated on September 2, 2026, the result is:

2

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The function returns an error if the supplied value is not a valid date.

An error also occurs if the required parameter is empty.

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
The day function can be combined with other date functions.

For example, you can extract the parts of an existing date and create a new date:

date(day(sourceDate), month(sourceDate), year(sourceDate) + 1)

This expression keeps the day and month from sourceDate and increases the year by 1.

You can also get the day of the month from a date calculated by another function:

day(dateshift(sourceDate, 10))

In this case, dateshift first calculates the new date, and day returns the day of the month from the resulting value.

docs.title: edate
docs.text:
The edate function shifts a date forward or backward by the specified number of months.

The function is useful when you need to calculate a date relative to another date, for example, to get a date several months later or determine a date in a previous period.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
edate(sourceDate, numberOfMonths)

Parameters:

  • sourceDate — the date from which the shift is calculated. Required;
  • numberOfMonths — the number of months by which the date should be shifted. Required numeric parameter.

A positive numberOfMonths value shifts the date forward, while a negative value shifts it backward. A value of 0 returns the original date without shifting it.

You can use:

  • field values;
  • results of other functions;
  • expressions.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns a date shifted by the specified number of months.

If the source date contains a time value, the time is preserved.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
If the target month does not contain the corresponding day, the function returns the last valid day of that month.

For example:

edate("31/01/2026", 1)

Result:

28.02.2026 00:00:00

The function accepts fractional numeric values.

For example:

edate(sourceDate, 1.5)

shifts the date forward by 2 months.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Shifting a date

edate("15/03/2025", 6)

Result:

15.09.2025 00:00:00

Using field values and an expression

If:

  • sourceDate = 15/03/2026;
  • numberOfMonths = 2;

the expression:

edate(sourceDate, numberOfMonths + 1)

returns:

15.06.2026 00:00:00

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The function returns an error if one of the required parameters is empty.

An error occurs if no value is provided for:

  • sourceDate;
  • numberOfMonths.

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
The edate function can be combined with other date functions.

You can create the source date using the date function and then shift it by the required number of months:

edate(date(15, 3, 2026), 6)

Result:

15.09.2026 00:00:00

The result of edate can be passed to a formatting function:

formatDate(edate(date(15, 3, 2026), 6),"dddd, d MMMM yyyy","en")

Result:

Tuesday, 15 September 2026

docs.title: eomonth
docs.text:
The eomonth function returns the last day of a month based on the specified offset from the source date.

The function is useful when you need to determine the end of the current, previous, or future month.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
eomonth(sourceDate, numberOfMonths)

Parameters:

  • sourceDate — the date used as the starting point for calculating the end of the month. Required;
  • numberOfMonths — the number of months to shift. Required numeric parameter.

A positive value shifts the calculation forward, a negative value shifts it backward, and 0 uses the month of the source date.

You can use:

  • field values;
  • results of other functions;
  • expressions.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns the date of the last day of the calculated month.

If the source date contains a time value, the time is preserved.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
The function automatically takes into account the number of days in each month.

For example:

eomonth("15/02/2025", 0)

Result:

28.02.2025 00:00:00

For a leap year:

eomonth("15/02/2024", 0)

Result:

29.02.2024 00:00:00

The function accepts fractional numeric values.

For example:

eomonth("15/04/2025", 1.5)

Result:

30.06.2025 00:00:00

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Shifting by several months

eomonth("15/04/2025", 2)

Result:

30.06.2025 00:00:00

Using an expression

If:

  • sourceDate = 15/04/2025;
  • numberOfMonths = 1;

the expression:

eomonth(sourceDate, numberOfMonths + 1)

returns:

30.06.2025 00:00:00

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The function returns an error if one of the required parameters is empty.

An error occurs if no value is provided for:

  • sourceDate;
  • numberOfMonths.

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
The eomonth function can be combined with other date functions.

You can create the source date using the date function and then determine the end of the required month:

eomonth(date(15, 4, 2025), 2)

Result:

30.06.2025 00:00:00

The result can be passed to a formatting function:

formatDate(eomonth(date(15, 4, 2026), 6),"dddd, d MMMM yyyy","en")

Result:

Saturday, 31 October 2026

docs.title: hour
docs.text:
The hour function returns the hour from a date and time value or a time value.

The function is useful when you need to extract the hour and use it separately in a document or expression.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
hour(value)

Parameters:

  • value — the date and time or time value from which the hour should be extracted. Required.

You can use:

  • a Date/Time or Time field value;
  • a text value containing a valid date and time or time;
  • the result of another function;
  • an expression whose result can be processed as a date or time.

For example, the function can process:

03/09/2026 15:53:21

or:

15:53:21

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns the hour as a number from 0 to 23.

For example:

hour("03/09/2026 15:53:21")

Result:

15

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Getting the hour from a time value

hour("15:53:21")

Result:

15

Getting the hour from a field value

If the signingTime field contains:

15:53:21

the expression:

hour(signingTime)

returns:

15

Getting the current hour

hour(now())

For example, if the current time is 15:53:21, the function returns:

15

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The function returns an error if the supplied value cannot be processed as a date or time.

An error also occurs if:

  • the required parameter is empty;
  • a plain numeric value is passed.

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
The hour function can be combined with minute and second to extract individual parts of a time value.

For example:

time(hour(sourceTime), minute(sourceTime), second(sourceTime))

If sourceTime contains:

15:53:21

the expression creates a time value with the same hours, minutes, and seconds.

docs.title: minute
docs.text:
The minute function returns the minutes from a date and time value or a time value.

The function is useful when you need to extract the minutes and use them separately in a document or expression.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
minute(value)

Parameters:

  • value — the date and time or time value from which the minutes should be extracted. Required.

You can use:

  • a Date/Time or Time field value;
  • a text value containing a valid date and time or time;
  • the result of another function;
  • an expression whose result can be processed as a date or time.

For example, the function can process:

03/09/2026 15:53:21

or:

15:53:21

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns the minutes as a number from 0 to 59.

For example:

minute("03/09/2026 15:53:21")

Result:

53

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Getting the minutes from a time value

minute("15:53:21")

Result:

53

Getting the minutes from a field value

If the signingTime field contains:

15:53:21

the expression:

minute(signingTime)

returns:

53

Getting the current minute

minute(now())

For example, if the current time is 15:53:21, the function returns:

53

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The function returns an error if the supplied value cannot be processed as a date or time.

An error also occurs if:

  • the required parameter is empty;
  • a plain numeric value is passed.

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
The minute function can be combined with hour and second to extract individual parts of a time value.

For example:

time(hour(sourceTime), minute(sourceTime), second(sourceTime))

If sourceTime contains:

15:53:21

the expression creates a time value with the same hours, minutes, and seconds.

docs.title: month
docs.text:
The month function returns the month number from a specified date.

The function is useful when you need to extract the month from a full date value and use it separately in a document or expression.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
month(date)

Parameters:

  • date — the date from which the month number should be extracted. Required.

You can use:

  • a date field value;
  • the result of another function that returns a date;
  • an expression whose result is a date.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns the month number as a value from 1 to 12.

For example:

month("11/08/2026")

Result:

8

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Getting the month from a field value

If the contractDate field contains:

11/08/2026

the expression:

month(contractDate)

returns:

8

Getting the current month

You can get the current month from the result of Today():

month(Today())

If the document is generated in September, the result is:

9

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The function returns an error if the supplied value is not a valid date.

An error also occurs if the required parameter is empty.

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
The month function can be combined with other date functions.

For example, you can extract the parts of an existing date and create a new date:

date(day(sourceDate), month(sourceDate), year(sourceDate) + 1)

This expression keeps the day and month from sourceDate and increases the year by 1.

You can also get the month number from a date calculated by another function:

month(edate(sourceDate, 6))

In this case, edate first calculates the new date, and month returns the month number from the resulting value.

docs.title: now
docs.text:
The now function returns the current date and time at the moment the document is generated.

The function is useful when you need to automatically insert the exact generation date and time or use them in calculations.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
now()

Parameters:

The function does not accept any parameters.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns the current date and time.

For example:

now()

Result:

02.09.2026 13:45:30

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
The function value is determined at the time the document is generated.

Unlike Today(), which returns the current date with the time set to 00:00:00, now() returns the current date and time.

For example:

Today()

Result:

02.09.2026 00:00:00

now()

Result:

02.09.2026 13:45:30

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Shifting the date and time

dateshift(now(), 1)

If now() returns:

02.09.2026 13:45:30

the result is:

03.09.2026 13:45:30

Shifting by one month

edate(now(), 1)

If now() returns:

02.09.2026 13:45:30

the result is:

02.10.2026 13:45:30

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
The result of now() can be used with other date and time functions.

For example:

formatDate(now(),"'Generated' dd.MM.yyyy 'at' HH:mm","en")

Result:

Generated 02.09.2026 at 13:45

docs.title: second
docs.text:
The second function returns the seconds from a date and time value or a time value.

The function is useful when you need to extract the seconds and use them separately in a document or expression.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
second(value)

Parameters:

  • value — the date and time or time value from which the seconds should be extracted. Required.

You can use:

  • a Date/Time or Time field value;
  • a text value containing a valid date and time or time;
  • the result of another function;
  • an expression whose result can be processed as a date or time.

For example, the function can process:

03/09/2026 15:53:21

or:

15:53:21

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns the seconds as a number from 0 to 59.

For example:

second("03/09/2026 15:53:21")

Result:

21

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Getting the seconds from a time value

second("15:53:21")

Result:

21

Getting the seconds from a field value

If the signingTime field contains:

15:53:21

the expression:

second(signingTime)

returns:

21

Getting the current second

second(now())

For example, if the current time is 15:53:21, the function returns:

21

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The function returns an error if the supplied value cannot be processed as a date or time.

An error also occurs if:

  • the required parameter is empty;
  • a plain numeric value is passed.

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
The second function can be combined with hour and minute to extract individual parts of a time value.

For example:

time(hour(sourceTime), minute(sourceTime), second(sourceTime))

If sourceTime contains:

15:53:21

the expression creates a time value with the same hours, minutes, and seconds.

docs.title: time
docs.text:
The time function creates a time value from separately specified hours, minutes, and seconds.

The function is useful when the parts of a time value are stored in different fields or calculated directly in an expression.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
time(hours, minutes, seconds)

Parameters:

  • hours — hours. Required. A numeric value from 0 to 23;
  • minutes — minutes. Required. A numeric value from 0 to 59;
  • seconds — seconds. Required. A numeric value from 0 to 59.

Parameters must be specified in the following order: hours, minutes, seconds.

You can use:

  • numbers;
  • values from numeric fields;
  • results of other functions;
  • expressions.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns a time value with the specified hours, minutes, and seconds.

In the full representation of the result, the technical date 01.01.0001 is used.

For example:

time(14, 30, 0)

Result:

01.01.0001 14:30:00

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Using field values and an expression

If:

  • hours = 13;
  • minutes = 30;
  • seconds = 0;

the expression:

time(hours + 1, minutes, seconds)

returns:

01.01.0001 14:30:00

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The function returns an error if one of the parameters is outside the allowed range.

For example:

time(24, 0, 0)

time(23, 60, 0)

time(23, 59, 60)

An error also occurs if one of the required parameters is empty.

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
The time function can be combined with other date and time functions.

For example, the hour, minute, and second functions can extract individual parts of the current time and use them to create a new time value:

time(hour(now()), minute(now()), second(now()))

To display the time without the technical date 01.01.0001, use formatDate:

formatDate(time(14, 30, 25), "HH:mm:ss")

Result:

14:30:25

docs.title: weekday
docs.text:
The weekday function determines the day of the week for a specified date and returns its number.

The function is useful when you need to determine the day of the week and use the result in conditions or other expressions.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
weekday(date, [returnType])

Parameters:

  • date — the date for which the day of the week should be determined. Required;
  • returnType — defines the first day of the week and the numbering system. Optional.

For the date parameter, you can use:

  • a Date field value;
  • a Date/Time field value;
  • a text value containing a valid date;
  • the result of another function that returns a date;
  • an expression whose result is a date.

The time component does not affect the day-of-week calculation.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns the day-of-week number.

If returnType is not specified, the following numbering is used:

Monday — 1
Tuesday — 2
Wednesday — 3
Thursday — 4
Friday — 5
Saturday — 6
Sunday — 7

For example:

weekday("03/09/2026")

Result:

4

because September 3, 2026 is a Thursday.

docs.title: Return type
docs.text:
The returnType parameter allows you to change the first day of the week and the numbering system.

Return type First day of the week Numbering 1 Monday 0–6 2 Tuesday 0–6 3 Wednesday 0–6 4 Thursday 0–6 5 Friday 0–6 6 Saturday 0–6 7 Sunday 0–6 11 Monday 1–7 12 Tuesday 1–7 13 Wednesday 1–7 14 Thursday 1–7 15 Friday 1–7 16 Saturday 1–7 17 Sunday 1–7

Return type 11 corresponds to the default numbering.

For example:

weekday("03/09/2026", 1)

Result:

3

With return type 1, Monday is numbered 0, so Thursday is numbered 3.

If return type 12 is used:

weekday("03/09/2026", 12)

the result is also:

3

In this case, Tuesday is the first day of the week and is numbered 1.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Checking whether a date falls on a weekend

If the date field contains:

05/09/2026

the expression:

weekday(date)

returns:

6

With the default numbering, 6 and 7 correspond to Saturday and Sunday.

For example, you can check whether a date falls on a weekend using:

weekday(date) >= 6

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The function returns an error if:

  • the required parameter is empty;
  • the supplied value cannot be processed as a valid date;
  • returnType contains a value other than 1–7 or 11–17.

For example, return type values 8, 10, and 18 return an error.

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
You can pass a date returned by another function to weekday.

For example:

weekday(now())

returns the number of the current day of the week.

The function can also be combined with date-shifting functions.

For example:

weekday(dateshift(sourceDate, 1))

First, dateshift calculates the date of the next day, and then weekday returns its day-of-week number.

docs.title: weeknum
docs.text:
The weeknum function determines the week number for a specified date.

The function is useful when you need to use the week number in a document, condition, or other expression.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
weeknum(date, [returnType])

Parameters:

  • date — the date for which the week number should be determined. Required;
  • returnType — a code that defines how weeks are calculated. Optional.

For the date parameter, you can use:

  • a Date field value;
  • a Date/Time field value;
  • a text value containing a valid date;
  • the result of another function that returns a date;
  • an expression whose result is a date.

For returnType, values from 11 to 17 and from 21 to 27 are supported.

If returnType is not specified, 11 is used.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns the week number as a number.

For example:

weeknum("12/08/2026")

Result:

33

The same result is returned when 11 is specified explicitly:

weeknum("12/08/2026", 11)

Result:

33

docs.title: Week numbering rules
docs.text:
Return types 11–17 and 21–27 use different rules for determining the first week of the year.

Return types 11–17

The week containing January 1 is considered the first week of the year.

The code defines the first day of the week:

  • 11 — Monday;
  • 12 — Tuesday;
  • 13 — Wednesday;
  • 14 — Thursday;
  • 15 — Friday;
  • 16 — Saturday;
  • 17 — Sunday.

For example:

weeknum("01/01/2022", 11)

Result:

1

Return types 21–27

With this numbering system, the first days of January may belong to the last week of the previous year.

The code also defines the first day of the week:

  • 21 — Monday;
  • 22 — Tuesday;
  • 23 — Wednesday;
  • 24 — Thursday;
  • 25 — Friday;
  • 26 — Saturday;
  • 27 — Sunday.

For example:

weeknum("01/01/2022", 21)

Result:

52

For the same date, return type 27 also returns:

52

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Getting the week number from a field value

If the documentDate field contains:

03/09/2026

the expression:

weeknum(documentDate)

returns:

36

Using a date and time value

The function can also process a value containing both a date and time:

weeknum("03/09/2026 15:53:21")

Result:

36

The time component does not affect the week number, which is determined by the date.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The function returns an error if:

  • the required parameter is empty;
  • the supplied value cannot be processed as a valid date;
  • returnType contains a value outside the supported ranges 11–17 and 21–27.

For example, return type values 10, 18, 20, and 28 return an error.

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
The weeknum function can be used with functions that return or modify dates.

For example, you can get the current week number using Today():

weeknum(Today())

You can also determine the week number after shifting a date:

weeknum(dateshift(sourceDate, 7))

First, dateshift calculates the new date, and then weeknum returns the week number for the resulting value.

docs.title: year
docs.text:
The year function returns the year from a specified date.

The function is useful when you need to extract the year from a full date value and use it separately in a document or expression.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
year(date)

Parameters:

  • date — the date from which the year should be extracted. Required.

You can use:

  • a date field value;
  • the result of another function that returns a date;
  • an expression whose result is a date.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns the year as a number.

For example:

year("11/08/2026")

Result:

2026

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Getting the year from a field value

If the contractDate field contains:

11/08/2026

the expression:

year(contractDate)

returns:

2026

Getting the current year

You can get the current year from the result of Today():

year(Today())

If the document is generated in 2026, the result is:

2026

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
The function returns an error if the supplied value is not a valid date.

An error also occurs if the required parameter is empty.

For example, if the field contains regular text instead of a date value, the function cannot extract the year from it.

docs.title: Related functions
docs.text:
The year function can be combined with other date functions.

For example, you can extract the parts of an existing date, change the year, and create a new date:

date(day(sourceDate), month(sourceDate), year(sourceDate) + 1)

This expression keeps the day and month from sourceDate and increases the year by 1.

You can also extract the year from a date returned by another function:

year(edate(sourceDate, 6))

In this case, edate first calculates the new date, and year returns the year from the resulting value.

docs.title: index
docs.text:
The index function returns a list item by its position.

List positions start at 1: the first item has position 1, the second has position 2, and so on.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
For a list with simple items:

index(list, position)

Parameters:

  • list — the identifier of the list field from which the item should be retrieved;
  • position — the position of the item. You can specify a number or an expression that returns a position.

For example:

index(stages, 2)

returns the second item from the stages list.

docs.title: List with Struct items
docs.text:
If the list contains Struct items, specify the identifier of the required nested field after the function using dot notation:

index(list, position).field

For example:

index(products, 2).name

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier;
  • 2 — the item position;
  • name — the nested field identifier.

docs.title: Getting an item by position
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field with the following identifier:

stages

The list contains:

Position Value 1 Preparation 2 Approval 3 Signing

The expression:

index(stages, 2)

returns:

Approval

Here:

  • stages — the list field identifier;
  • 2 — the item position in the list.

docs.title: Getting a field from the first item that matches a condition
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field:

products

Each list item is a Struct field containing:

  • name — the identifier of the product name field;
  • price — the identifier of the product price field.

The list contains:

Position name price 1 Chair 3500 2 Desk 7500 3 Cabinet 12000

You need to get the name of the first product with a price greater than 5000.

Expression:

index(
    products,
    match(
        product in products,
        product.price > 5000
    )
).name

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier in the template;
  • product — the name of the current item defined inside the match function;
  • price — the nested field identifier;
  • match(...) — returns the position of the first matching item;
  • index(...) — returns the item at that position;
  • name — the field of the matching item whose value should be returned.

The match function checks the items in order:

3500 > 5000 → false
7500 > 5000 → true

The second item is the first one that matches the condition, so the expression effectively becomes:

index(products, 2).name

Result:

Desk

docs.title: Getting a value from the last item in a list
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field:

payments

Each list item is a Struct field containing:

balance

You need to get the balance value from the last item in the list, while the number of items is not known in advance.

Expression:

index(
    payments,
    count(payment in payments)
).balance

Here:

  • payments — the list field identifier;
  • payment — the name of the current item defined inside the count function;
  • count(...) — returns the number of items in the list;
  • the returned value is used as the position of the last item;
  • balance — the nested field identifier whose value should be returned.

If the list contains four items:

count(payment in payments)

returns:

4

The expression then effectively becomes:

index(payments, 4).balance

and returns the balance value from the last item in the list.

docs.title: avg
docs.text:
The avg function calculates the arithmetic mean of numeric values from list items.

A numeric field or an expression can be used as the value for the calculation.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
avg(item in list, expression)

Parameters:

  • item — the current list item;
  • list — the identifier of the list field;
  • expression — a numeric value or expression whose result is included in the arithmetic mean calculation.

docs.title: List with Struct items
docs.text:
If each list item is a Struct field, you can assign any valid name to the current item and use it to access nested fields.

For example:

avg(product in products, product.price)

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier;
  • product — the name of the current item defined directly in the function;
  • price — the nested numeric field identifier;
  • product.price — the value used to calculate the arithmetic mean.

You can choose the name of the current item yourself. For example, instead of product, you can use item:

avg(item in products, item.price)

docs.title: List with simple items
docs.text:
If the list contains simple numeric values, the current item itself is used in the expression.

Suppose the ratings list contains numeric values.

Expression:

avg(rating in ratings, rating)

In this case, each value in the list is used directly in the calculation.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text: The function returns a number — the arithmetic mean of the expression results for all items in the list.

docs.title: Calculating the average product price
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field with the following identifier:

products

Each item is a Struct field containing:

  • name — product name;
  • price — product price.

The list contains:

name price Monitor 15000 Keyboard 800 Printer 12000 Mouse 600

To calculate the average product price, use:

avg(product in products, product.price)

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier;
  • product — the name of the current item defined inside the avg function;
  • price — the numeric field identifier inside the item;
  • product.price — the value retrieved from each list item.

Result:

7100

docs.title: Calculating the average of a simple numeric list
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field:

ratings

The list contains:

4
5
3
5

Expression:

avg(rating in ratings, rating)

returns:

4.25

docs.title: Calculating the average result of an expression
docs.text:
The second parameter can also contain an expression.

Suppose the products list contains:

  • name — product name;
  • price — unit price;
  • quantity — product quantity.

Source data:

name price quantity Monitor 15000 2 Keyboard 800 5 Printer 12000 1 Mouse 600 10

You need to calculate the average total cost of a product line based on its quantity.

Expression:

avg(product in products, product.price * product.quantity)

For each item, the function first calculates the line total:

name Calculation Value Monitor 15000 × 2 30000 Keyboard 800 × 5 4000 Printer 12000 × 1 12000 Mouse 600 × 10 6000

The function then calculates the arithmetic mean of these values.

Result:

13000

docs.title: count
docs.text: The count function determines the number of items in a list.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
count(item in list)

Parameters:

  • item — the name of the current list item. It is defined directly in the function;
  • list — the identifier of the list field whose items should be counted.

For example:

count(product in products)

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier in the template;
  • product — the name of the list item defined directly in the function.

You can choose the item name yourself. It is used only inside the function expression.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text: The function returns an integer — the number of items in the list.

docs.title: Counting list items
docs.text:
Suppose the template contains a list field with the following identifier:

products

The list contains:

Position Name 1 Monitor 2 Keyboard 3 Printer 4 Mouse

Expression:

count(product in products)

returns:

4

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier;
  • product — the name of the list item defined inside the count function.

docs.title: Counting items that match a condition
docs.text:
The count function can be applied to a list returned by filter.

Suppose the products list contains:

name price Monitor 15000 Keyboard 800 Printer 12000 Mouse 600

You need to determine how many products have a price greater than 5000.

Expression:

count(
    product in filter(
        item in products,
        item.price > 5000
    )
)

Here:

  • products — the identifier of the source list field;
  • item — the name of the current item inside the filter function;
  • item.price > 5000 — the filtering condition;
  • filter(...) — returns a new list containing only matching products;
  • product — the name of an item in the filtered list inside the count function.

After filtering, the list contains:

Monitor — 15000
Printer — 12000

Therefore, count returns:

2

docs.title: Getting the last item in a list
docs.text:
The result of count can be used as an item position in the index function.

Suppose the template contains a list field:

payments

Each list item contains the following field:

balance

You need to get the balance value from the last item in the list, while the number of items is not known in advance.

Expression:

index(
    payments,
    count(payment in payments)
).balance

Here:

  • payments — the list field identifier;
  • payment — the name of the list item inside the count function;
  • count(...) — returns the number of items in the list;
  • the returned number is used by index as the position of the last item;
  • balance — the nested field identifier whose value should be returned.

For example, if the list contains four items:

count(payment in payments)

returns:

4

The expression then effectively becomes:

index(payments, 4).balance

and returns the balance value from the last item in the list.

docs.title: filter
docs.text: The filter function selects list items that match a specified condition.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text:
filter(item in list, condition)

Parameters:

  • item — the name of the current list item. It is defined directly in the function and used in the condition;
  • list — the identifier of the list field;
  • condition — a Boolean expression that determines whether the current item should be included in the result.

You can choose the name of the current item yourself. It is used only inside the function.

For example:

filter(product in products, product.price > 5000)

Here:

  • products — the list field identifier;
  • product — the name of the current item defined inside the function;
  • price — the nested field identifier;
  • product.price > 5000 — the filtering condition.

Only products with a price greater than 5000 are included in the result.

docs.title: Return value
docs.text:
The function returns a new list containing only the items for which the condition returns true.

The original list is not changed.

The result of filter(...) can be used instead of the original list:

  • in a for or t_for block;
  • in other list functions;
  • in aggregate functions such as count, sum, avg, min, and max.

This allows you to filter the required items first and then perform calculations only on those items.

docs.title: Outputting only matching list items
docs.text:
